Good idea. Buggy Implementation. The app got a lot of good features. While most financial institutions offer their own consolidated and financial planning tools, they often fall short of what I needed so I have resorted to using my own spreadsheets and manually updating them regularly. I was hoping Origin will eliminate that, but unfortunately it’s still not a very mature product. For one thing it is buggy in many places and hence I can’t fully trust it. It is also rather simplistic in how it deals with budgeting and expenses. There’s little to no room for actual customization. Also, as a an already retired person, I found the app to completely ignore my situation (for example it keeps making irrelevant suggestions.) In summary, the app has potential but for now, I’m still relying on my spreadsheets.

Your data is not safe. YOU ARE THE PRODUCT - NOT THE DASHBOARD. PROTECT YOUR DATA.

At first I was experiencing a bug that logged me in to blank dashboards, so I filed a ticket. After weeks of back and forth, zero progress. However, months later, I  am still getting notifications about my financial activity, with zero dashboard access. Under state law, they’re required to delete my data on my request. After 3 weeks, I have no access to my data, and they are still ingesting all of my activity. 

Now origin is able to sell my financial activity data to the highest bidder while me, the paying “customer,” receives zero value. They refuse to delete my data. This isn’t only unethical, it’s illegal. Be wary.

I only paid $1 for a promotional year, but the app is just sitting on my phone taking up space. I am definitely canceling my subscription before it expires because it offers absolutely no value when you actually need financial help. They have a lot of bugs to fix before this is worth paying for.
